message.content: {"caption":"Few-shot adaptation workflow: demonstration grids prompt a model to specify self-edit settings, whose augmented examples are used for fine-tuning before the updated model is tested on a new grid.","description":"A left-to-right workflow titled “Few-Shot Setup” sits on a light rounded background. On the left, “Few-Shot Examples” contains five horizontal pairs of small cell grids. The grids show different arrangements of dark blue, blue, and teal cells, with some empty cells. A right-pointing arrow leads to a box labeled “LM θ_t.” A branching connector from this model leads into two yellow self-edit settings boxes under “Self-Edit (SE).” The upper box reads “basic_augmentations: true,” “size_augmentations: false,” “chain_augmentations: false,” and “repeat_augmentations: false.” The lower box reads “strategy: loss on all tokens,” “learning rate: 1e-05,” and “epochs: 3.” To their right, a large blue-outlined panel contains multiple small blue-and-teal grid patterns representing generated or augmented examples. A downward arrow from this panel points to a training expression. A right-pointing arrow from the settings leads through a purple “SFT” box to a loss expression showing a grid batch and θ_t as inputs, followed by a right-pointing arrow to θ′_t. A vertical divider separates the “Evaluation” section on the right: a small blue-and-teal grid input points right to “LM θ′_t,” which points right to another colored grid. A check mark above the output grid marks it as correct. No crosses are shown.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
